answers.children: Yes — Irish Red and White Setters are good with children thanks to their gentle nature and affectionate temperament. Their large athletic build and high energy require supervision during rough play but they carefully interact with toddlers using their fieldwork poise. The breed's stamina and intelligence help them engage in games without becoming overwhelming when given proper outlets. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Irish Red and White Setters generally get along with other pets because of their friendly disposition and sociable temperament. Bred for pointing and retrieving rather than pursuing quarry they show low prey drive around household animals although same-sex tension can appear if not introduced carefully.
answers.exercise: Irish Red and White Setters need two hours of vigorous daily exercise including off-leash runs and fieldwork simulations. Without this their high energy leads to destructive chewing or digging as the athletic build craves the miles of rough terrain it was developed to cover in Ireland. Scent games and structured hunts suit their intelligent hunter heritage.
answers.shedding: Yes — Irish Red and White Setters shed moderately year-round with heavier seasonal sheds. Their medium silky coat carries feathering that traps loose hair on furniture and clothing while the elegant patches require regular removal of undercoat to limit tracking from their active fieldwork lifestyle.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Irish Red and White Setter is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. The medium silky coat with its feathering still releases dander and loose hair during activity making it unsuitable for those sensitive to canine proteins despite the breed's elegant appearance.
answers.training: Irish Red and White Setters are moderately easy to train because their intelligence and biddability allow quick learning of commands when motivated by fieldwork tasks. Their high energy and affectionate drive respond best to positive methods that channel the stamina originally bred for pointing and retrieving game birds.
answers.lifespan: Irish Red and White Setters live 11-15 years. Their large athletic build and exceptional stamina support an active life yet the breed's health robustness score reflects vulnerability to certain genetic issues that can influence longevity in this elegant Irish hunter.
answers.size: Irish Red and White Setters reach 45-70 lb and stand 22-26 in tall. The substantial yet elegant build with fluid movement feels like a lively houseful of dog that needs space to stretch its long-legged frame developed for covering Irish hills and marshes.
answers.barking: Irish Red and White Setters do not bark a lot. Their quiet nature stems from the focused hunting background where excessive noise would disturb game and the low barking score reflects minimal vocalising except when separation anxiety surfaces after hours alone or during intense boredom that leads to other unwanted behaviours.
answers.apartment: No — Irish Red and White Setters do not suit apartment living well. Their high energy and need for vigorous daily runs combined with the tendency to become destructive when under-stimulated make settling indoors difficult for this large athletic breed originally developed for fieldwork across open Irish terrain.
answers.first-time: No — Irish Red and White Setters are not a good first dog. Their high energy demands consistent outlets and structured training to prevent destructive habits while the affectionate yet intense temperament requires experienced handling to manage the stamina and intelligence of this rare Irish hunting breed.
